key_insight: Quantum measurement noise can replace part of the randomness required by diffusion sampling, reducing measurement shots rather than merely suppressing noise.
engineering_relevance: State-dependent shot budgets offer a route to lower quantum sampling costs while preserving diffusion generation quality.
method: Model finite-shot readout error as multinomial noise propagated through a trainable linear readout.
Formulate diffusion on a bounded zero-sum hyperplane mapped to the probability simplex.
Add compensation noise to match the ideal linear update’s mean and covariance, deriving an adaptive minimum shot budget.
evidence_signal: On an eight-dimensional Gaussian mixture, the method achieved comparable generation quality using 303 shots per sample versus a 1.6-million-shot reference—about 5,300× fewer—with additional validation on MNIST latent diffusion.
watch_item: Moment matching requires minimum shot conditions, and the DDIM shot budget rises as sampling becomes more deterministic.
paper_title: Leveraging Quantum Measurement Randomness for Shot-Efficient Diffusion Models
